Do not cause difficulty to the people (because they are afraid to perform Tawaaf with you here), it would be best for you to remain at home." she then remained at home (and stopped going to the Masjidul Haraam). It later occurred that a man passing by her said to her, "The person who had prevented you has passed away. You may now come out." She responded by saying, "It is not befitting of me to obey him while he was alive and then disobey him after his death."
sources: Hannaad, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai .3 Pg.165). (4) tbn jareet. as quoted in Kanzul Ummaai. 3 Pg,i68).

paras: Hadhrat Shamar narrates from a man who had been the chief of an area during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Ali (RA) that Hadhrat Ali is once issued an order to them and then asked, "Will you do as you have been ordered?" when the said that they would not, Hadhrat Ali (RA) said, "I swear by Allaah that you must do as you have been commanded otherwise the Jews and the Christians will definitely mount you necks."
Hadhrat Urwa bin zubayr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once sent (!) From Sayf bin Amr, also narrating from Hadhrat Hasan.

Hadhrat Arnr bin Al Aas (RA) (as Ameer) on a military expedition to the rural towns of Shaam, where the Battle of Dhaatus Salaasil was fought. The towns were those of the Banu Baliy tribe, the Banu Abdullaah tribe and the Banu Qudaa'ah tribe next to them. It was from the Banu Baliy tribe that the maternal uncles of Aas bin waa'il hailed (Aas bin Waa'il was the father of Hadhrat Amr bin Aas. When Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) arrived at the place, he was apprehensive of the large numbers of the enemy and sent a message to Rasulullaah ﷺ asking for reinforcements.

Rasulullaah ﷺ prepared the early Muhaajireen for the task and amongst the most senior Muhaajireen who got ready for the task were Hadhrat Abu Bakr and Hadhrat umar (RA). Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah as their Ameer and when they met Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas, he said to them, "I am your Ameer now for I had sent the message to Rasulullaah ﷺ asking for you to come here as reinforcements. However, the group of Muhaajireen said, "You may be the Ameer of your army, but our Ameer is Abu ubaydah Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas ffi reiterated what he said by saying, "You are only the reinforcements that I had requested." Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) was a man of excellent character and very soft-hearted. When he saw what was happening, he said, 'You ought to know O Amr that the parting instruction Rasulullaah ﷺ gave to me was, 'When you reach your companion, co-operate with him.' I shall therefore obey you even if you wish to disobey me." With this, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) handed over the commend to Hadhrat Amr (RA). (RA)

Another narration from Zuhri states that Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched two expeditions against the Banu Kalb tribe, the Ghassaan tribe and other Kuffaar tribes located in the rural towns of Shaam. Rasulullaah ﷺ appointed Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah as Ameer of one expedition and Hadhrat Amr bin (RA) Aas as Ameer of the other. Marching in the army of Hadhrat Abu ubaydah was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and Hadhrat Umar (RA). when the two armies were about to leave, Rasulullaah fflefflig called for Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah and Hadhrat Amr (RA) and said to them, "Never oppose each other." When the two armies had left (Madinah), Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) took Hadhrat Amr (RA) aside and said to him, "Rasulullaah ﷺ had emphatically advised us never to oppose each other, it is either you who will obey me or t that will obey you," Hadhrat Amr (RA) replied, "I'd rather that you obey me." Hadhrat Abu ubaydah (RA) then accepted to be under the command of Hadhrat Amr (RA), who became the commander of both armies. Hadhrat Umar (RA) became angry at this arrangement and said (to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah, "You have chosen to be under the command of Naabigha's son and have made him your Ameer, the Ameer of Abu Bakr and our Ameer?!" what sort of idea is this?" Hadhrat Abu ubaydah (RA) pacified Hadhrat umar (RA) by saying, "Dear brother! Rasulullaah ﷺ emphatically advised me and Amr never to oppose each other I therefore feared that if I do not obey him, I would be disobeying Rasulultaah. In this way, more people would be the cause of spoiling my relationship with Rasulullaah ﷺ. 1 swear by Allaah that 1 shall now obey him until we return." When they returned from the expedition, Hadhrat Umar (RA) complained about this to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "After this, 1 shall appoint only someone from yourselves Muhaajireen) as your Ameer."

Hadhrat Salama bin Shihaab Abdi reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once said, "O citizens! We (leaders) have a right that you owe to us. It is that you always wish well for us even in our absence and that you assist us in all good works. Take note that there is nothing more beloved to Allaah and which has a more widespread benefit than the tolerance and compassion of an Ameer towards his subjects. On the contrary, there is nothing more detested by Allaah than the foolishness of an Ameer and his harshness," ' Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Akeem states that Hadhrat Umar said, "There is no tolerance more loved by Allaah than the tolerance and compassion of an Ameer (towards his subjects). There is also no foolishness that is more detested by Allaah than the foolishness and harshness of an Ameer. Those who overlook things that happen to him will receive health and safety and those who exercise justice between people even when it concerns himself shall be granted success in his affairs. Suffering disgrace when being obedient is closer to goodness than winning honour through sin."

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates, "The senior companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ used to prevent us from certain misdeeds. They would say, 'Never speak ill of your leaders, never betray them and never disobey them. Fear Allaah and exercise patience because the event (Qiyaamah/death) is close by."
Refraining from Speaking the Truth Before Leaders.

Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that he once approached Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar bin Khattaab and said, "O Abu Abdur Rahmaan! Sometimes we sit with these leaders of ours and we confirm what they say even though wc know that it is not true. Even when they make unjust decisions, we still support them and make it seem credible to them. What do you think about this?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar said, "Dear nephew! During the time we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ we regarded this to be an act of hypocrisy but I do not know what you regard it to be." ' '

Another narration from the father of Hadhrat Aasim bin Muhammad states that someone once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA), "When we are with our leaders, wesaythingsthatare quite the opposite of what we say when we leave them," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) commented, ,rWe used to regard this as an act of hypocrisy." Bukhari has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Muhammad bin Zaid but adds that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) said, "During the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, we regarded this to be an act of hypocrisy." Hadhrat Mujaahid reports that when a man came to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar the latter asked him, "How is the relationship between you people and Abu Unays (the Ameer)?" The man replied, "Our relationship is that when we meet with him, we tell him what he likes to hear and sing a different tunc when we go away from him." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) commented, "when we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ, this is the thing we regarded as hypocrisy."
sources: Ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzu! Ummaa! Pg.93).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that they once said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar "When we enter the courts of these people (our leaders), we say the things they like to hear but then say the opposite when we leave their presence." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin (RA) said, "During the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ, wc used to regard this as an act of hypocrisy."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.4 Pg.332). uayhaqi (Vol.8 Pg.165).

paras: Hadhrat Alqama bin Waqqaas narrates that there was a useless man who used to enter the courts of the governors and make them laugh. Hadhrat Alqama's grandfather said to the man, "Shame on you! why do you enter the courts of these people and make them laugh?! I have heard from Bilaal bin Haarith who was a companion of Rasulullaah f)SSI that Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'A servant (of Allaah) may utter a word that pleases Allaah without him realising its true potential and because of it, Allaah becomes pleased with him until the day he meets Allaah. On the contrary, a servant (of Allaah) may utter a word that displeases Allaah without him realising its true potential and because of it, Allaah becomes displeased with him until the day he meets Allaah.'"'ss Another narration from Hadhrat Alqama states that Hadhrat Bilaal bin Haarith (Vol. 8 Pg., as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.4 Pg.382).

Muzani said to him, "I see that you enter the courts of these governors and overwhelm them. Do check what you are saying to them because 1 have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, " A servant (of Allaah) may utter a word..." The rest of the narration is like the one mentioned above.

Hadhrat Hudhayfa (RA) once said, "Beware of the dens of evil!" "What are the dens of evil, O Abu Abdullaah?" someone enquired from him. He replied, "The doors of the rulers. A person enters the court of a ruler and then confirms the lies he speaks and praises him for qualities he does not possess."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) narrates that his father (Hadhrat Abbaas once said to him, "Dear son I notice that the Ameerul Mu'mineen calls for you, allows you to be close to him and even consults with you together with the Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ. Now remember these three things that I am telling you. Fear Allaah and never let him encounter any lies from you (never tell him a lie). You should also never disclose any of his secrets and never backbite about anyone in his presence." One of the narrators by the name of Aamir says that he said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas iS "Each one of these advices are belter than a thousand." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) in turn said, "Each one of them is better than ten thousand."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.227).

paras: Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) once said to his son Hadhrat Abdullaah, "1 notice that that great man (referring to Hadhrat Umar allows you to sit close to him and includes you amongst people with whom you do not belong (the veterans of Gadr). You should therefore remember three things that I shall tell you. Never let him encounter any lies from you, (never tell him a lie), never disclose any of his secrets and never backbite about anyone in his presence."

Hadhrat Hasan (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once refused to accept a verse or the Qur'aan from Hadhrat Ubay (RA) (saying that it is either not in the Qur'aan or not as Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said it appeared). (RA) Ubay said, "I had heard it from Rasulullaah ﷺ at a time when you were preoccupied with trade in Baqee." Hadhrat umar (RA) then said, "You have spoken the truth, (t knew that the verse is in the Qur'aan but I refused to accept it because) I only wanted to test whether there are people amongst you who would speak the truth (before the Ameer). There is no good in an Ameer in whose presence the truth cannot be spoken and who does not speak the truth."
sources: Surah Maa 'id ah, verse 107.

paras: Hadhrat Abu Mijlaz reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) accused Hadhrat Ubay of lying when he recited the versed Hadhrat Ubay (RA) retorted by saying, "Your lie is worse!" Someone reprimanded Hadhrat Ubay (RA) by saying, "Are you calling the Ameerul Mu'mineen a liar?" Hadhrat ubay (RA) replied, "I have more respect for the rights of the Ameerul Mu'mineen than you have. However, 1 have falsified him only to confirm the truth of Allaah's Book and I can never confirm what the Ameerul Mu'mineen says when it entails falsifying the Book of Allaah." Hadhrat Umar then said, "He has spoken the truth.
sources: Abd bin Hurr,ayd, Ibn larcer and Adi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal Pg 285). (4) ibn Asaakir and Abu Dharr Harawi in his Majaami. as quoted in Kanzul Pg. 148).

paras: Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) reports that in a gathering of Muhaajirecn and Ansaar, Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked, "What will you people do if I were permissive in certain matters?" when everyone remained silent, Hadhrat Umar repeated the question for a second and then a third time. Hadhrat Basheer bin Sa'd then responded by saying, "If you do that, we will set you straight as an arrow is straightened." Hadhrat Umar (RA) commented, "You are then certainly the ones (capable of being with me You are then certainly the ones!"

Hadhrat Moosa bin Abu Isa narrates that when Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab went to the pond of the Banu Haaritha, he met Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama there. Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him, "What do you think of me?" Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) replied, "I swear by Allaah that in my opinion you are as 1 like to see you and as anyone who likes good likes to see you. 1 see that you are meticulous in collecting wealth, are also abstinent from it (1) Ibn Raahway, as quoted in Kanzul ' Ummaai '(Vol.7 Pg.2). and distribute it justly. If however, you stray, we shall straighten you just as arrows are straightened with weights." Hadhrat umar (RA) then said "Excellent! (You say,) 'if however, you stray, we shall straighten you just as arrows are straightened with weights'. All praise belongs to Allaah Who has placed me amongst people who will rectify me when I stray." !

Hadhrat Abu Qabcel narrates that Hadhrat Mu'aawiya Sii'SKs once ascended the pulpit on the day of Jumu'ah and said in his lecture, "The wealth is all ours and the spoils of war are all ours. We shall give it to whom we will and refuse whoever we will." Since no one responded to this statement, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya repeated it the following Jumu'ah. When no one objected this time as well, he again repeated it on the third Jumu'ah. On that occasion, a man in the Masjid stood up and said, "Never! The wealth is ours and the spoils of war are ours. If anyone poses an obstacle between us and it, we shall have him dealt with by Allaah or by our swords."

After Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) descended from the pulpit, he sent for the man, who was allowed in his court. "He is destroyed!" the people commented. However, when the people entered the court of Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA), they found the man sitting with Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA) on his bed. Hadhrat Mu'aawiya then said to the people, "This man has given me life, may Allaah give him life. 1 have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Soon after me there shall come rulers who will say (wrong) things and no one would object to them. They will fall over each other in Jahannam just as monkeys (jumping from a tree) fall over each other.' when no one objected to what ! said on the first Jumu'ah, I feared that I would be amongst these rulers. When no one objected on the second Jumu'ah, I said to myself that I must be from amongst them. However, when I spoke on the third Jumu'ah, this man objected. He has given me life, may Allaah give him life."
sources: lbn Mubaarak, as quoted in Muntakhah Kanzui Ummaal'.

paras: Hadhrat Khaalid bin Hakeem bin Hizaam reports that when Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah was governor of Shaam, he punished some of the local (Kuffaar) persons (for not paying the Jizya(3)). Hadhrat Khaalid bin waleed (RA) stood up and spoke to him (about the error of his act). The people commented, "You have made the Ameer angry." Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) said, "I had never intended to make him angry but I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that the people who will be most severely punished on the Day of Qiyaamah will be those who punished people most severely in this world."
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzv! Ummaa! (Vol. 3 Pg.166). Tabari (Vol. 5 Pg.33) has also reported a similar narration,

paras: Hadhrat Hasan reports that when Ziyaad dispatched Hadhrat Hakam bin Amr Ghifaari as governor of Khurasan, the Muslims there managed to win a large amount of booty. Ziyaad then wrote to Hadhrat Hakam (RA) saying, "The Ameerul Mutnineen (Hadhrat Mu'aawiya (RA)) has written to say that all the gold and silver should be reserved for him and should therefore not be distributed amongst the Muslims." Hadhrat Hakam (RA) wrote back to Ziyaad saying, "You have written to me about the letter of the Ameerul Mu'mineen: However, I have received the Book of Ailaah before the letter of the Ameerul Mu'mineen (1 shall therefore not obey his command which contradicts that of the Qur'aan). I swear by that even if the skies and earth have to close up on a person, Ailaah will create an escape for him between them and give him peace if he is one who fears Ailaah."

Hadhrat Hakam (RA) then had an announcer announce to the people that they should present themselves for the booty by the morning. He then distributed the booty (including the gold and silver) amongst the people. When he did this, Hadhrat Mu'aawiya is sent some people to arrest Hadhrat Hakam (RA) and place him in shackles. Hadhrat Hakam (RA) passed away in these shackles and was buried in Khurasan. He said, "l shall contest (my case against Mu'aawiya ig in the court of Another narration adds that after Hadhrat Hakam (RA) had distributed the booty amongst the people, he prayed, "O Ailaah! If You have any good for me with You, then raise me to You." He then passed away in the town of Maroo in Khurasan. Isaaba (Vol.1 Pg.347) states that it was actually when Hadhrat Hakam received the letter of Ziyaad noting his displeasure, he prayed to Ailaah (for a swift death), after which he passed away.

Hadhrat Ataa reports that-Ziyaad or his son once sent Hadhrat Imraan bin Husayn to collect Zakaah. When Hadhrat Imraan (RA) returned, he brought nothing back. "Where is the money?" asked Ziyaad (or his son). "Did you send me to bring back any money?" Hadhrat Imraan (RA) asked, "I collected it as we used to do during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ and used it in the avenues we used it during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ (1 distributed it amongst the needy of the area)."
sources: Hannaad, as quoted in Kanzui Pg.166).

paras: Hadhrat Aswad bin Yazeed narrates that whenever a delegation came to Hadhrat umar, he would ask them about their governor. He would ask, "Does he visit the ill? Does he respond to the pleas of slaves? How does he treat those who stand at his door (to have a need fulfilled)?" if the delegates had to give a negative answer to any of the questions, Hadhrat umar (RA) would dismiss the governor. '''

Hadhrat Ibraheem reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) appointed a governor to an area and a delegation had to come to him from the same area, he would ask them, "How is your governor? Does he visit the slaves? Does he follow funeral processions? How is his door (is he accessible)? is it welcoming?" If the people replied that the governor's door was welcoming and that he visited the slaves, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would leave the man in his post. Otherwise, he would send a messenger to dismiss him.
sources: Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.3 fg.148).

paras: Hadhrat (RA) states that whenever Hadhrat umar' dispatched governors, he would make the conditions with them that they should never ride Turkish horses, should not eat refined white flour, should not wear fine clothing and should not lock their doors to those who were in need. He made it clear to them that if they were ever to do any of this, they would be liable for punishment. It was only after making these conditions that he saw them off (walked a distance with them), when he was about to return, he would further tell them, "l ■ am not sending you to give you sovereignty over the blood of people, over their skins, over their honour and over their wealth. I am sending you to ensure that the people establish salaah, to distribute the spoils of war amongst them and to judge between them with justice, if you encounter any difficulties, do refer it to me. Beware that you never hit an Arab for this would humiliate them. Never prevent them from returning to their homelands because this would place them in great difficulty and never level false accusations against them because you would then be depriving them (of their rights). Also ensure that you keep the (words of the) Qur'aan separate (from the Ahadeeth and from commentaries so that these are nor confused as part of the Qur'aan)." $)

Another similar narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Keep the Qur'aan separate and report fewer narrations from Rasulullaah ﷺ. 1 shall also join you in doing this." Hadhrat Umar (RA) would also enforce the necessary punishment on his governors (when they deserved it) and whenever a complaint was brought to him about any governor, he would gather the complainant and the governor in one place. Thereafter, if the complaint was proven to be valid and the governor needed to be taken to task, Hadhrat Umar (RA) would take him to task.

Hadhrat Abu Khuzayma bin Thaabit (RA) reports that whenever Hadhrat umar appointed someone as governor, he would make a group of the Ansaar and some others witness (to the appointment) and say (to the new governor), "I am not sending you to give you sovereignty over the blood of people..." The rest of the narration is similar to the one quoted earlier.
sources: Tabari (Vol. 5 Pg.19).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Saabit reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent for Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Aamir Jumhi (RA) and said to him, "We wish to appoint you in command of this regiment whom you should lead into enemy territory to wage war with them," Hadhrat Sa'eed SE said, (RA) Umar! Please do not try me." Hadhrat Umar (RA) resolved "I shall never leave you. You people have cast this responsibility (of Khilaafah) on my neck and now you wish to leave me all alone! I am sending you with a group of people from whom you are not the best. I am not sending you to whip them or to humiliate them but only to lead them in jihaad against their enemies and to distribute their booty amongst them." ,3)

Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) once addressed the people saying, "The Ameerul Mu'mineen Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) has sent me here to teach you the Book of your Rabb, the Sunnah of your Nabi ﷺ and to administrate over municipal affairs."
sources: Rm-Abi Sbaybah, as quoted in Kamul Ummas/. 3 Pg.148).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Saalih Ghifaari narrates that Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) (while in Egypt) once wrote to Hadhrat Umar (RA) stating: "We have reserved a house for you here next to the Jaami Masjid." Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote back saying. "Why should a man living in Hijaaz have a house in Egypt?" Hadhrat umar (RA) then ordered that the area be converted into a marketplace for the Muslims.
sources: )bn Abdul Hakam. as quoted in gamut Ununaal Pg.l48l.

paras: Hadhrat Tameem jayshani (RA) reports that Hadhrat umar (RA) wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Amr bin M Aas (RA)

"The news has reached me that you have had a pulpit made by which you climb high above the people's necks (when delivering a sermon), is it not sufficient for you to remain standing with the Muslims beneath your heels. 1 command you in the name of Allaah that you should demolish it."
sources: Ibn Abdul Hakam. as quoted in Uinmaa! Pg.166).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote a letter to them when they were in Azerbaijan. He wrote: "O Utba bin Farqad! Your position and wealth has not been the fruits of your efforts, nor the fruits of your father's or mother's efforts. Feed the people in their homes with that which you feed yourself in your home. Guard yourself against indulging in luxuries, from imitating the appearance of the Mushrikeen and from wearing silk clothing."
sources: Muslim, as quoted in Targheeb wat Tarheeb (Vol.3.

paras: Hadhrat urwa bin Ruwaym narrates lhat Hadhrat umar (RA) was inquiring about the condition of the people (during the Hay) when some people from Hims passed by him. "How is your Ameer?" asked Hadhrat umar (RA). They replied, "He is the best of Ameers except for the fact that he had built a lofty residence in which he lives.

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote a letter, which he sent with a messenger with instructions to burn the building down, when the messenger reached Hims, he gathered firewood and set fire to the door. When the Ameer was informed about it, he said, "Leave him alone because he has been sent (by the Ameerut Mu'mineen)." The messenger then handed the letter over to the Ameer, (After reading the letter) The Ameer did not even put the letter down when he rode off to Hadhrat Umar (RA). When Hadhrat Umar iI saw him arrive, he told the Ameer to meet him at Harra where the Zakaah camels were kept. (When he met him there) Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him to remove his clothes and then gave him a garment of camel hide to wear. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed him to fetch water from the well to give the camels to drink. The man continued going in and out of the well until he was exhausted. Hadhrat Umar then asked him, "How much longer will you be in this world?" "For only a short while," came the reply. Hadhrat umar (RA) commented, 'Then is it for this short while that you have built the mansion and adopted a standard of living that exceeds those of the poor, the widows and orphans? Go back to your post and never repeat yourself."

Hadhrat Attaab bin Rifaa'ah narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once received the news that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) had built a mansion and had a door put on it, saying that the noise from the marketplace has now been cut off (form entering the mansion), Hadhrat Umar (RA) then dispatched Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama, whom he always sent when he needed a task done exactly as he wanted. The instructions he gave Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) was to bring Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) to him and to burn down the door. (When Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) arrived in Someone cameto Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) and informed him (about the arrival) and when the features (of Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA)) were described to Hadhrat Sa'd (RA), he recognised him, Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) then went to meet Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA), who said to him, "The news has reached the Ameerul Mu'mineen that you commented about the noise being cut off." When Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) swore that he never made such a statement, Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) said, "We shall do as we have been commanded while you will have to convey what you said (to the Ameerul Mu'mineen)."

When Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) offered to provide Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama with provisions for the journey, he refused to take any and rode off until he reached Madinah. when Hadhrat Umar (RA) saw him, he said, "if I did not have a good opinion of you, I would have thought that you did not fulfil the task," Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) informed Hadhrat Umar (RA) that he had hurried back and assured Hadhrat umar (RA), "I have fulfilled the task. However, Sa'd excuses himself and swears that he had never made the statement,"

Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Did he give you any provisions for the journey?" Hadhrat Muhammad bin Maslama (RA) replied, "No, but what prevented you from giving me provisions?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I disliked giving you any provisions because although you would have had ease, I would have had to suffer for it (in the Aakhirah) since hunger is killing the people around me in Madinah. Have you not heard Rasululiaah say that a Mu'min should not fill his belly while his neighbour goes hungry?" jVol-2) 121 .another narration from Iladhrat Abu Bakrah and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah states that the news that reached Hadhrat Umar (RA) stated that Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) kept aloof from the people and locked them out of his house. Hadhral Umar then dispatched Hadhrat Ammaar bin Yaasir Si with instructions to go to Hadhrat Sa'd Si and if he found the door locked, he was to burn il down.
sources: Abu Dawood arid Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzti! tyo Pg,l48).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once sought permission from Hadhrat umar (RA) to go to Shaam. Hadhrat Umar (RA) told him that he would be allowed to go there onlyoncondition that he became a governor of one of the areas. When Hadhrat Abu Dardaa refused to be a governor, Hadhrat Umar (RA) refused to grant the permission. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) then said, "I shall go there to teach people the Sunnah of their Nabi ﷺ and lead them in salaah." Hadhrat Umar then granted him permission.

Hadhrat Umar (RA) later visited Shaam and when he drew close to where the Sahabah (RA) were staying, he stopped until evening fell. When the night cast its veil over him, he called to his slave saying, "O Yarfa! Let us go to Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan, You will see that he has story-tellers with him, lanterns will be burning and rugs of silk and velvet will be spread out, which have been taken from the booty belonging to the Muslims, You will greet him and he will reply, after which you will ask permission to enter and he will not grant permission until he enquires who you arc."

The two men proceeded until they reached the door of Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Sufyaan. Hadhrat Umar (RA) greeted by saying, "As Salaamu Alaykum!" to which Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) replied, "Wa Alaykumus Salaam," When Hadhrat Umar JUls/iSei asked whether he could enter, Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) first asked, "who arc you?" To this Yarfa replied, "This is the one who is about to spoil your fun. This is the Ameerul Mu'mineen." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then opened the door and found story-tellers there, lanterns burning and rugs of silk and velvet. Hadhrat Umar (RA) urgently instructed Yarfa to shut the door and struck Hadhrat Yazeed (RA) with his whip right between the ears. Hadhrat Umar then folded up all the goods and placed it at the centre of the room. He then issued the command that no one should move until he returned. Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Yarfa then left Hadhrat Yazeed (RA). Hadhrat Umar entire narration is reported in Isaaba (Vol .3 pg.384) except that the narrator's name appears as Abaaya bin Rtfaa'ari instead of Attaabbin Rifaa'ah. Haythami (vol. 8 Pg.i67) has commented on the chain of narrators. said, "O Yarfa! Come with me to Amr bin Al Aas. You will see that he has story-tellers with him, lanterns will be burning and rugs of velvet will be spread out, which have been taken from the booty belonging to the Muslims. You will greet him and he will reply, after which you will ask permission to enter and he will not grant permission until he enquires who you are." The two men proceeded until they reached the door of Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas Hadhrat Umar (RA) greeted by saying, "As Salaamu Alaykum!" to which Hadhrat Amr (RA) replied, "wa Alaykumus salaam." when Hadhrat Umar asked whether he could enter, Hadhrat Amr (RA) first asked, "Who are you?" To this Yarfa replied, "This is the one who is about to spoil your fun. This is the Ameerul Mu'mineen." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then opened the door and found story-tellers there, lanterns burning and rugs of velvet. Hadhrat Umar (RA) urgently instructed Yarfa to shut the door and struck Hadhrat Amr (RA) with his whip right between the ears. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then folded up all the goods and placed it at the centre of the room. He then issued the command that no one should move until he returned.

After leaving Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "O Yarfa! Let us go to Abu Moosa Ash'ari. You will see that he has story-tellers with him, lanterns will be burning and rugs of wool will be spread out, which have been taken from the booty belonging to the Muslims. You will greet him and he will reply, after which you will ask permission to enter and he will not grant permission until he enquires who you are."

The two men proceeded until they reached the door of Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari. Hadhrat Umar (RA) greeted by saying, "As Salaamu Alaykum!" to which Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) replied, "Wa Alaykumus Salaam," when Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked whether he could enter, Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) first asked, "Who are you?" To this Yarfa replied, "This is the one who is about to spoil your fun. This is the Ameerul Mu'mineen." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then opened the door and found story-tellers there, lanterns burning and rugs of wool spread out. Hadhrat Umar (RA) struck Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) with his whip right between the ears and then said, "You too, O Abu Moosa (have you also changed since leaving Madinah)?" Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! This is what I have (which is less than the others) You have already seen what my companions are doing whereas I had also received what they have received (but have not gone to the extent they have)." Hadhrat Umar asked, 'Then what is all this about?" Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) replied, "The people of the city believe that this is the only way by which to rule." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then folded up all the goods and placed it at the centre of the room. He then.issued the command that no one should move until he returned.

When the two had left Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA), Hadhrat umar (RA) said, "0 Yarfa! Come with me to my brother (Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA)). You will see that he has no story-tellers with 'him, no lanterns will be burning and his (Vol-2) 123 door will be unlocked. You will greet him and he will reply, after which you will ask permission to enter and he will grant you permission without enquiring who you are."

The two men proceeded until they reached the door of Hadhrat Abu Dardaa 5S.13SSJ9. Hadhrat Umar (RA) greeted by saying, "As Salaamu Alaykum!" to which Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) replied, "Wa Alaykumus Salaam." When Hadhrat Umar asked whether he could enter, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) granted permission. As Hadhrat Umar (RA) pushed open the door, he found that it had no lock. The two men entered the dark room and Hadhrat umar (RA) had to feel his way around until he found Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA). When Hadhrat Umar felt the pillow of Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), he found that it was made from the blanket used on animals. When he felt the ground, there was only sand and .when he felt the clothing of Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA), he discovered that it was a flimsy shawl.

Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) asked, "Who is this? is it the Ameerul Mu'mineen?" When Hadhrat Umar (RA) confirmed that he was the Ameerul Mu'mineen, Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, 'You are late. We had been waiting for you all year." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, (RA) have mercy on you. Have I not granted you sufficient wealth? Have I not given you plenty?" Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "o Umar! Do you not remember a Eladith that Rasulullaah ﷺ mentioned to us?" "Which lladith?" asked Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Abu Dardaa replied, "(The Hadith in which Rasulullaah ﷺ said,) 'The limit of a person's possessions in this world should be like the provisions of a traveller.'" "Oh yes (l have heard the Hadith)" confirmed Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Abu Dardaa then asked, "Now what have we done after Rasulullaah ﷺ, O Umar?" The two Sahabah (RA) then continued reminding each other (of the words of Rasulullaah ﷺ. with tears in their eyes until morning arrived.

Hadhrat Abu Saalih Ghifaari narrates that there was an extremely old blind lady living on the outskirts of Madinah whom Hadhrat Umar (RA) used to regularly visit at night. He would go there to fetch water for her (from the well) and do other chores for her. However, whenever he got to her, he would find that someone else had beat him there and had already seen to her needs. He went to her many times only to find that he was not the first to get there. (One day) He sat in wait for the person (who always beat him) and found that the person was Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) would tend to the old lady even though he was the Khalifah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, "By my life! It could only be you!"

Hadhrat Awzaa'ee reports that Hadhrat Talha (RA) once spotted Hadhrat Umar coming out (of his house) late at night. Hadhrat Umar (RA) entered a house and then another house. The following morning, Hadhrat Talha (RA) went to the house, where he found an old woman who was blind and crippled. Hadhrat Talha (RA) asked her, "why does that man come to you?" She then informed Hadhrat Talha (RA) that Hadhrat Umar (RA) had been frequently coming to her for many years to see to her needs and remove all the filth from her house. Hadhrat Talha Si! then said to himself, "Shame on you, O Talha! Were you searching for faults in umar?!"

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Utba bin Mas'ood says that he heard Hadhrat Umar say, "People would be taken to task by, means of revelation during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ (when Allaah would send revelation to disclose the secrets of some people). However, revelation has been terminated and now we are able to take you people to task by your apparent actions. Therefore, we will trust and bring close to us only those people whose apparent actions appear good to us because we have no knowledge of his inner self. Allaah is the One Who will take him to task for his inner condition. On the other hand, we cannot trust and cannot believe those whose apparent actions appear evil to us even though he may claim that his inner condition is good."

Hadhrat Hasan states that in the first lecture that Hadhrat Umar (RA) delivered (after becoming the Khalifah), he first praised Ailaah and then said: "(Now that 1 have become Khalifah) I am being tested through you people and you will be tested through me, l have been made the Khalifah after my two companions and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). We shall therefore deal directly with those in our presence and to deal with those who are not in our presence, we shall appoiat over them people who are capable and trustworthy. We shall treat well those people who do good and punish those who do evil. May Allaah forgive you and I."

Hadhrat Tawoos narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked (the people), "Tell me whether I would be discharging my responsibility if I appoint over you a person who is the best of you in my knowledge and then 1 command him to be just?" "Most certainly," came the reply. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said, "No (1 would still not have discharged my responsibility), unless I inspect whether or not he is doing what I have commanded him to do."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ka'b bin Maalik Ansaari that a regiment of the Ansaar were posted to Persian territory with their Ameer. Although Hadhrat Umar would continuously dispatch troops every year (to relieve others), he happened to be preoccupied (with other tasks) and failed to relieve the particular regiment. When their term expired, the troops posted at that border (the regiment of Ansaar) returned. Hadhrat Umar (RA) became very angry and threatened action against them (because he had not yet sent anyone in their place). They all happened to be Sahabah (RA) of Rasulullaah ﷺ and they said, "O Umar! You were too preoccupied to worry about us and failed to implement the command of Rasulullaah ﷺ to continuously dispatch troops." The Consideration the Ameer ought to Give to the people when they are Faced with a Problem The Incident between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) During the Plague of Airovaas Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) narrates that as soon as the Ameerul Mu'mineen (Hadhrat umar (RA)) heard about the plague that was affecting the people in Shaam, he wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA)

"I require you to fulfil a need I have and I cannot do so without you having it fulfilled, if this letter of mine reaches you at night, \ emphatically command you not to let the morning arrive without you riding off to me (in Madinah). If this letter of mine reaches you in the morning, i emphatically command you not to let the evening arrive without you riding off to me."

(After reading the letter) Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) remarked, "I know well what need has presented itself to the Ameerul Mu'mineen, He wishes to preserve someone who cannot remain living (he wants me to escape the plague by returning to Madinah)." Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) then wrote back to Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying: "I am part of a Muslim army. I am not prepared to leave them to save my own life. I am weil aware of the need that has presented itself to you. You wish to preserve someone who cannot remain living. When this letter of mine reaches (1)Bayhaqland, as quoted in Kanzu! Ummaal tyo Pg,l65). you, do absolve me of your command and permit me to remain here,"

When Hadhrat Umar (RA) read this letter, his eyes welled with tears and he began to weep. The people with him asked, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Has Abu Ubaydah passed away?" "No," replied, Hadhrat Umar (RA), "but it is as if he already has." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote back to Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah t saying: "Indeed the entire land of Jordan has been affected by the epidemic whereas the region of Jaabiya is free from it. You should therefore take the Muhaajireen there."

When Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah t had read the letter, he said, "We shall certainly listen to and obey this command of the Ameerul Mu'mineen," Hadhrat Abu Moosa reports further, "Abu Ubaydah then ordered me to mount my animal and to keep the people in their living quarters. In the meantime, my wife also got affected by the plague. When 1 reported this to Abu Ubaydah he personally proceeded to confine the people to their quarters, after which he was also afflicted and passed away. The plague then came to an end."
Hadhrat Abul Muwajjih says, "It is believed that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) was part of an army of thirty six thousand people. Every one of them save six thousand died."
sources: lbn Abi Shaybah, as quoted in Kanzvl Ummaal Pg.229). (2) lbn Mundhir, Haakim and Bayhaqi, as quoted in K3p7.ul Umsnaal '(Vol.2 Pg.226).

paras: Another narration states that (when he read the letter from Hadhrat Umar Hadhrat Abu ubaydah (RA) said, "May Allaah forgive the Ameerul Mu'mineen. He wishes to preserve the lives of people who cannot remain living (forever)." Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) then wrote back to Hadhrat Umar saying, "Verily, I am with an army from amongst the armies of the Muslims whom 1 am not prepared to leave to save my own life from that which had afflicted them." Yet another narration states that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) wrote to Hadhrat Umar saying: "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I knew well your need from me. However, I am part of a Muslim army that I do not wish to leave to save my own life. I have no desire to leave them until Allaah passes His decree concerning me and concerning them. O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Do release me from your command (to return to Madman) and leave me with my army."
sources: Bayhaqi (Vol.9 Pg.41) and Hannaad. as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal ' (Vol.3 Pg.165).

paras: Hadhrat Abu ja'far reports that Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA) once brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ some captives from Bahrain, Looking at a woman from amongst them weeping, Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, "What is the matter?" She replied, "He has sold my son." "Have you sold her son'" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked.
(1)lbnAsaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Umuiaal Pg.324)

"Yes," replied Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA). "To which tribe?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked further. Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA) replied, "To the Banu Abs tribe." Rasulullaah then instructed Hadhrat Abu Usayd (RA) saying, "Ride to them and bring him back yourself."

Hadhrat Buraydah (RA) narrates that he was sitting with Hadhrat Umar (RA) one day when he heard a scream. Hadhrat Umar (RA) instructed his slave Yarfa to see where the noise was coming from. After checking, Yarfa reported, "The mother of a girl from the Quraysh is being sold (as a slave, because of which the child is screaming)." Hadhrat Umar is then instructed him to summon the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar. After a short while, the room and the entire house was filled. After praising Allaah, Hadhrat Umar (RA) then said: "Do you people know whether the severing of family ties was amongst the teachings that Rasulullaah ﷺ brought?" When they replied in the negative, Hadhrat Umar Mi continued, "Because it has started to spread rapidly amongst you." He then recited the following verse of the Qur'aan: It is possible that if you are given authority (to rule over others), you would spread corruption on earth and (let alone harming others, you would even) sever family ties. (Surah Muhammad ﷺ, verse 22) Hadhrat Umar JD'SSSs continued, "What form of severing family ties is worse than selling the mother of a girl from amongst you when Allaah has given you abundance?" The Sahabah (RA) said, 'Do as you see fit." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then wrote to all the regions (of the Islaamic Empire) instructing that the mother of no free woman should be sold a slave) because it entails severing family ties which is not permissible.

Hadhrat Abu Uthmaan Nahdi reports that after Hadhrat Umar (RA) had appointed a man from the Banu Asad tribe as governor, the man came to him to collect the certificate of appointment. In the meantime, one of Hadhrat Umar children was brought to him and he started kissing the child. The man from the Banu Asad tribe asked, "Do you kiss children, O Ameerul Mu'mineen? By Allaahl I have never kissed a child to this day." Hadhrat Umar then said, "In that case, I swear by Allaah that you will be even less compassionate towards people. Give the certificate of appointment back. You should never act as governor for me ever again." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then cancelled his appointment. * '

A narration of Hadhrat Muhammad bin Sallaam states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said (to the man), "what trime is it of mine that mercy has been extracted from your heart? Allaah has mercy only on those servants of his who show mercy." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then removed him from the post and said, "If you have no mercy for your own children, how will you have mercy on the masses?"'

Hadhrat Urwa (RA) narrates that in the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ a woman stole during the conquest of Makkah. The members of her tribe (the Banu Makhzoom) hurried to Hadhrat usaama bin Zaid (RA) to ask him to intercede (on her behalf before Rasuluilaah so that her hand should not be cut off), when Hadhrat Usaama (RA) spoke about it to Rasulullaah ﷺ, Rasulullaah face turned red (with anger) and he said, "Are you talking to me about (waiving) a penalty that Allaah has imposed?" Hadhrat Usaama (RA) cowered and said, "Seek Allaah's forgiveness for me, O Rasulullaah ﷺ That evening, Rasulullaah ﷺ stood up to deliver a lecture. After duly praising Allaah, he said: "The nations before you were destroyed because whenever a noble person amongst them stole, they let it be. However, when a weak person (from a family holding no status) stole, they imposed the penalty on him, l swear by the Being Who controls my life that even if Faatima the daughter of Muhammad ﷺ has to steal, I would cut off her hand."

Rasulullaah ﷺ then issued the necessary instructions and the woman's hand was cut off. She then repented sincerely to Allaah and even got married. Hadhrat Aa'isha says, "Thereafter, she used to come to me and I would present her needs to Rasulullaah ﷺ.
sources: Daynowri, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol.8 Pg,3l0).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Qataadah (RA) reports, "After we had left with Rasulullaah ﷺ for the Battle of Hunayn and met with the enemy, we suffered a temporary defeat. When 1 saw a man from the Mushrikeen overpowering one of the Muslims, I used my sword to strike his subclavian vein (on the shoulder) from behind. My blow cut through his armour and he turned to me. He then grabbed hold of me and started squeezing me so hard that I could get the smell of death. Fortunately, (because he had lost a lot of blood,) death" overcame him and he Set go of me. I then met Hadhrat umar (RA) and asked, "What has happened to the people (Why did the Muslims suddenly flee)?' He replied, 'it was the command of Allaah.' (However, the Muslims then regrouped and fought back to defeat the Mushrikeen). When the Muslims returned (from the battlefield, Rasulullaah ﷺ sat down and said, "Whoever killed someone and has a witness to testify shall have the possessions of the dead man.' 1 stood up and asked, 'Who will testify for me?' (When I received no response) l sat down again, when Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated the announcement, 1 again stood up and asked, will testify for me?' (When I again received no response) 1 sat down. Rasulullaah ﷺ repeated the announcement and again 1 stood up and asked, 'Who will testify for me?' (When I received no response this time) I sat down yet again. When Rasulullaah again repeated the announcement, I stood up. Rasulullaah ﷺ asked, 'What is the matter, O Abu Qataadah?' After I had informed him of the incident, someone said, 'He had spoken the truth and the dead man's possessions are with me. O Rasulullaah ﷺ Satisfy him on my behalf (give him something else so that i may keep the possessions).' Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then said, 'Never! By Allaah! In that case, whenever one of the lions of Allaah fight for Allaah and His Kasool, should he give you what is taken from the enemy?1 Rasulullaah confirmed what was said by saying, 'He is right. Hand over the possessions.' The man handed me the possessions and with it i bought an orchard in the Banu Salma district. This was the first time that I had received any wealth as a Muslim."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad Aslami (RA) narrates that he owed four Dirhams to a Jewish man, who then complained about him (to Rasulullaah ﷺ) saying, "0 Muhammad ﷺ That man owes me four Dirhams but he keeps overpowering me (refuses to pay whenever I ask him). Rasulullaah ﷺ said to Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad (RA), "Pay this man his dues," Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad replied, "l swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that 1 cannot pay him." "Pay this man his dues," Rasulullaah repeated. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad (RA) pleaded, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life that I am unable to pay him. I have already informed him that you would soon send us to Khaybar from where I hope to return with some spoils of war that you give us. I would then be able to pay him back with this." However, Rasulullaah ﷺ again instructed, "Pay the man his dues." It was the habit of Rasulullaah ﷺ that he never repeated anything after the third time something three times meant that it was final). Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad (RA) then proceeded to the marketplace. He was wearing a turban on his head and a shawl as his lower garment. He removed the turban from his head and used it as a lower garment. He then removed the shawl and said (to the jew), "Buy this shawl from me." The Jew bought it from him for four Dirhams. An old woman then passed by and asked, "What is the matter, O companion of Rasulullaah ﷺ when Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abu Hadrad related the incident to her, she took off a shawl she was wearing and threw it over him saying, "Take this shawl."
sources: Asaakir. as quoted in Kanzui Ummaai Pg.lSl). Ahmad has reported a similar narration, as quoted in (Vol.2.

paras: Hadhrat ummu Salama (RA) reports that two men from the Ansaar brought to Rasulullaah ﷺ their dispute concerning some inheritance for which they could produce no evidence nor any witnesses. Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them, 'You are bringing your dispute to me when I can pass judgement only by my estimation in matters concerning which no revelation has come to me. Therefore, if I decide in the favour of someone because of his stronger case, thereby severing any right of his brother, he should not accept it. In that case. i would be apportioning for him a part of Jahannam. on the Day of Qiyaamah he will come with it as a yoke around his neck."

The two men started weeping and each one of Lhem said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I hand over my right to him." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Since you want it that way, go and ponder about the right, divide it between yourselves and draw lots (to decide who should have which share). Each one of you should then permit his share for the other (so that none stands responsible for taking the right of the other)."

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed (RA) reports that a Bedouin once came to Rasulullar'i to demand payment of a debt Rasulullaah ﷺ owed to him. He behaved very harshly with Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "I shall continue plaguing you until you pay the debt!" The companions of Rasulullaah ﷺ admonished the man saying, "Shame on you! Do you know with whom you arc talking?!" The man said, "I am only asking for my right." Rasulullaah ﷺ said to them, "Why are you not defending the one who has a right?"

Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent for Hadhrat Khowia bint Qais (RA) and asked her, "Borrow me some dates if you have any and 1 shall pay you back when I receive some dates." She said, "Most certainly! May my parents be sacrificed for you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ She then borrowed the dates to Rasulullaah ﷺ, with which he paid the Bedouin off together with something extra. The man then said, "You have given me full payment, may Allaah give you in full." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "They are the best of people (who support those with a right). There is no good in a nation whose weak people cannot claim their right without hesitation."
sources: Tbn Abi Shaybah and Abu Sa'eed tv'aqqaash, as quoted in Kanzui Ununaaitycti.'i Pg.182).

paras: Hadhrat Khowla bint Qais (RA) who was the wife of Hadhrat Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib narrates, "Rasulullaah ﷺ owed a Wasaq of dates to a man from the Banu Saa'idah tribe. When the man came to claim repayment, Rasulullaah ﷺ instructed someone from the Ansaar to pay it. When the Ansaari paid the man in dates which were of an inferior quality, he refused to accept it. The Ansaari said, "Are you refusing Rasulullaah ﷺ The man said, "Yes. Who is more worthy of exercising justice than Rasulullaah ﷺ Rasulullaah ﷺ eyes welled with tears as he said, "He is right. Who is more worthy of exercising justice than me? May Allaah not bless a nation whose weak ones cannot claim their rights from their powerful ones and cannot demand them either." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said, "O Count and settle his debt because when a creditor is satisfied when he leaves his debtor, all creatures on earth and fish in the oceans pray for him (the debtor). However, when a debtor delays in paying when he has the means to pay, Allaah records a sin in his records for every day and night that passes (without him paying)."
sources: A unit weigh! equal to approximately 25 kg.
Tabraani avid Ahmad, as quoted in Targheeb wat rarheeb (Vol.3 Pjj.270), narrating from reliable sources.

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Al Aas reports that Hadhrat Abu Bakr stood up one Friday and announced, "Bring the Zakaah camels tomorrow morning so that we may distribute them. Remember that none should come to see us without permission." A woman said to her husband, "Take this rein (to be given with the camels to the poor). Perhaps Allaah shall make it a means of providing a camel for us." The man arrived at a time when Hadhrat Abu Bakr and Hadhrat Umar (RA) were with the camels and entered (the enclosure) with them. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) turned around and asked, "Who allowed you to come here?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then took the rein from the man and hit him with it. After he had completed distributing the camels, Hadhrat Abu Bakr summoned the man and handing him the rein, said, "Take your revenge." Hadhrat Umar (RA) quickly intervened and said, "By Allaahr He should not take revenge from you. You should not make this a custom (that people should take revenge from an Ameer who needs to teach a lesson to people)." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "Then who will defend me in Allaah's court on the Day of Qiyaamah?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "Compensate him somehow." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) then instructed his slave to give the man a riding camel together with its carriage and blanket. In addition to this, he also gave him five Dinaars (gold coins). In this manner, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) secured the man's pardon.

Hadhrat Sha'bi reports that a dispute arose between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Appoint someone to decide the matter between us." They then agreed to appoint Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (to settle the matter) between them. When the two men came to Hadhrat Zaid (RA), he made place at the head side of his bedding saying, "Sit here, O Ameerul Mu'mineen," Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "That is the first wrong you have committed in your decision-making procedure. I shall rather sit with my contestant." The two men then sat in front of Hadhrat Zaid (RA). Hadhrat Ubay made his claim and Hadhrat Umar (RA) refuted it, Hadhrat Zaid then said to Hadhrat Ubay (RA), "Absolve the Ameerul Mu'mineen (from taking an oath, which is the next step of the procedure since no witnesses were presented). I would not have asked for 'this concession for anyone else besides the Ameerul Mu'mineen." However, Hadhrat umar (RA) still took the oath and then said, "Zaid will be unable to judge unless he treats Umar as a man from the ranks of the common Muslims." The narration of lbn Asaakir states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b disputed about the harvesting of a date crop. With tears in his eyes, Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "is this how it will be under your rule, O Umar?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Then appoint someone to decide between us." When Hadhrat ubay (RA) suggested the name of Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit Si Hadhrat Umar (RA) accepted and the two of them went to him. The rest of the narration is like the one above.
sources: lbn Asaakir. Sa'eed bin Mansoor and Bayhaqi.

paras: Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam reports that Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) had a house next to the Masjid of Madinah. Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) to sell the house to him because he intended adding it to the Masjid. However, Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) refused to sell it. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) requested him to give it as a gift, Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) refused this as well. Hadhrat Umar said, "You have no option but to accept one of the two proposals." When Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) still refused, Hadhrat Umar (RA) told him to appoint someone (to decides the matter between them). Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) appointed (U Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaa! (Vol. 3 Pg. 127).

Hadhrat Ubay (RA) and the two men took their case to him. (After hearing the case,) Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "I do not see any way in which you can remove him from his house without his consent," Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Tell me whether you found this judgement in the Book of Allaah or in a Hadith of Rasulullaah ﷺ "it is in a iladith of Rasulullaah ﷺ replied Hadhrat ubay (RA). when Hadhrat umar asked for substantiation, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said, "I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that while Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA) the son of Hadhrat Dawood was constructing Baytul Maqdas, he found the walls destroyed every morning after he had them built. Allaah then sent revelation telling him that he would be unable to build anything on the land of another person without the person's consent."

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once intended to take the house of Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) to include it in the Masjid. However, Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) refused to hand the house over. When Hadhrat Umar resolved that he would certainly have possession of the house, Hadhrat Abbaas proposed that they appoint Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) to pass judgement between them. Hadhrat Umar (RA) agreed and they both approached Hadhrat Ubay (RA). After they had related the matter to him, Hadhrat Ubay (RA) said, "Allaah sent revelation to Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Dawood instructing him to construct the Baytul Maqdas. The land belonged to a man whom Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA) approached to buy it from him. However, when Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA) handed over the money to the man, he asked, 'is this price that you are paying better or is that which you are taking from me better?' Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA) replied, 'Certainly that which I am taking from you is better.' 'in that case,' said the man, 'I shall not accept it.' Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA) then gave the man a higher price. The man then did the same thing two or three times until Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA) made a condition with him, 'I am buying this land from you at the price you fix. You may therefore not ask me which of the two is better.' Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA) took the purchased land from him at the price he fixed, which happened to be twelve thousand Qintaar of gold (one Qintaar equals four thousand gold coins). Hadhrat Sulaymaan then felt that the amount was too big to give the man. Allaah then sent revelation to him saying, 'If you are paying him from something that is your own, then you know best (what you have to do). However, if you are paying him from what We have provided for you, then give him whatever he is pleased with.' Hadhrat Sulaymaan (RA) then paid the amount."

Hadhrat ubay (RA) continued, "I feel that Abbaas has a greater right to his house, which cannot be taken from him until he is pleased." Hadhrat Abbaas then said, "Since you have made the decision in my favour, I wish to make it Sadaqah for the Muslims."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq. 1 34 (Vol-2)

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin umar (RA) reports that his brother Abdur Rahmaan and Abu Saroo'ah both drank some wine while they were in Egypt during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat Umar (RA). They were both intoxicated and the following morning they approached Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) who was the Ameer of Egypt. They said to him, "Purify us (by imposing the penalty) because we had both become intoxicated with what we drank."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "when my brother mentioned to me that he had become intoxicated, l said to him, 'Come into the house and I will purify you.' 1 did not know then that he had already been to Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas. when my brother told me that he had already informed the Ameer of Egypt, I said, Your head will not be shaved in front of all the people today. Go into the house and 1 will myself shave your head.' The practice of governors in those days was that they shaved the heads of criminals together with imposing the penalty. The two men then entered the house. ; shaved my brother's head with my own hand and then Hadhrat Amr (RA) hi: j them lashed." Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) continues, "When Hadhrat Umar (RA) heard about this, he wrote to Hadhrat Amr (RA) with instructions to send Abdur Rahmaan to him on a carnage. Hadhrat Amr (RA) complied and when Abdur Rahmaan reached (his father) Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) lashed him and punished him further because of his relationship with him. Hadhrat Umar then let him go and he lived hail and healthily for a month after which his predestination caught up with him and he passed away. Although people commonly believe that he died because of the lashing he received from Hadhrat Umar (RA), it is evident that he did not die because of this lashing."
sources: Abdur Razzaaq and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzu/ Uimnaa/fVolA l'g.422), narrating from reliable sources, ibn Sa'd has also reported the narration in detail from Aslam who narrates from Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA), as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol .4 Pg.420).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once sent for a woman whose husband had gone missing. Hadhrat Umar (RA) objected to the fact that (!) Abdur Kazzaaq, as quoted in fianzul Ummaal (Vol.4 Pg.260), Ibn Sa'd (Vol.4 Pg.13) has reported a similar narration, Ibn Asaakir has also reported a similar narration in great detail from Saalim Abu Nadhar and the chain of narrators are reliable save for the fact that Saalim was not a contemporary of Hadhrat Umar (RA). Bayhaqi and Ya'qoob bin Sufyaan have reported the narration briefly from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) with a reliable chain of narrators, as quoted in Kanzu! ummaal (Vol.7 Pg-65). in this narration, Hadhrat rfudhayfa (RA) is mentioned instead of Hadhrat Ubay S3!S!eSS. people used, to frequently visit her. when she was summoned, it was said to her, "Respond to Lhe call of Umar." She bemoaned, "Alas! 1 am destroyed! What docs Umar want with me?!" (She was pregnant and) As she was still on her way, she became so frightened that labour pains struck. She entered a house where the urir ^ ^ /-hiM nnlu and it Umar said, "You killed him because of his intentions! Which of us does not make intentions (to do evil)? Had it not been for the fear that it would become routine, I would have killed you for (killing) him."

Hadhrat Zaid bin Wahab narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once emerged from his home with his fingers in his ears and saying, "If only I could have been at your service! If only I could have been at your service!" When the people asked what the matter was, Hadhrat Umar (RA) informed them that a messenger had come to him from one of his governors stating that a river presented an obstacle to the progress of their army and they could not find a boat to cross over. The Ameer of the army instructed the others to find a man who knew how to gauge the depth of a river. They brought an old man who pleaded to the Ameer saying, "I fear the cold." Although it was winter, the Ameer forced him to go into the river and it was not long before the cold overcame him and the last thing he shouted before he drowned was, "Help me, O Umar!"

Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote to the Ameer (to come to Madinah) and when he arrived, Hadhrat Umar (RA) ignored him for a few days. Hadhrat Umar (RA) usually did this when he was angry with someone. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked him, "What wrong was done by the man you killed?" The Ameer said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I never intended to kill him. Because we could find nothing with which to cross over, we only wanted to ascertain the depth of the water." He then went on to enumerate the many territories they had conquered. However, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "A single Muslim is more valuable to me than all your achievements. Had I not feared that it would become a common practice, I would have executed you. Pay the Diyah to his family and go somewhere where I would not see you again."
sources: lbn Abdul Hakam, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.298).

paras: Hadhrat Jareer narrates that a man who was 'with Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (in a battle) managed to gain a large booty. Although Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari gave the man some share of the booty, it was not the complete share. The man refused to accept anything less than his complete share. Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari then gave the man twenty lashes and shaved off his hair. The man collected his hair and went to Hadhrat Umar (RA). He then took out the hair from his pocket and thrust it on Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s chest. "What is the matter?" asked Hadhrat Umar (RA). After the man recounted the incident to Hadhrat Umar (RA), the Khalifah wrote a letter to Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari. After greeting Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA), Hadhrat Umar wrote the name of the person who had informed him of the incident and also wrote the details of what he heard. Thereafter, he wrote: "I order you in the name of Allaah that if you had carried out the act in public, you should sit in public and allow him to have his revenge from you. If you had done so in private, then you should sit in private and allow him to have his revenge." when this letter reached Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA), he sat down for the man to take his revenge, but the man said, "I have forgiven him for the pleasure of Allaah."
Hadhrat Hirmaazi reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote the following letter to Hadhrat Fayrooz Daylami (RA)
"The news has reached me that you are very occupied with eating refined bread with honey. When this letter of mine reaches you, come to me in the name of Allaah and fight in the way of Allaah."

When Hadhrat Fayrooz Daylami (RA) arrived (in Madinah), he sought permission to see Hadhrat Umar (RA) and permission was granted. Just then, he was about to enter) a youngster from the Quraysh also rushed in and jostled Hadhrat Fayrooz (RA). Hadhrat Fayrooz (RA) lifted his hand and slapped the Qurayshi on the nose. The Qurayshi entered the presence of Hadhrat Umar with a bleeding nose and Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked him, "Who did this to you?" "Fayrooz," came the reply. Hadhrat Fayrooz (RA) was still standing at the door and then entered after Hadhrat Umar (RA) gave him permission to do so.

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked, "What is this, O Fayrooz?" he replied, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! It was just recently that we had been kings. You had written to me (to come here) but did not write to him. You had also permitted me to enter and did not permit him. However, he wanted to enter before me with the permission I had been granted. I then did what he has informed you about." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Retribution!" "Does it have. to be?" asked Hadhrat Fayrooz. "It will have to be," Hadhrat Umar (RA) confirmed. Hadhrat Fayrooz then knelt on his knees and the youngster stood ready to have his revenge. Hadhrat Umar (RA) interrupted by saying, "Hold it boy until I inform you about what I heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say one morning. He said, 'Last night Aswad Anasi the great liar (who claimed to be a Nabi) was killed last night. It was the pious servant Fayrooz Daylami who killed him.' Can you see yourself taking revenge from him after hearing this from Rasulullaah ﷺ The youngster said, "I have forgiven him after you have informed me about this statement of Rasulullaah ﷺ Hadhrat Fayrooz (RA) then asked Hadhrat Umar (RA), "Tell me whether my admission to guilt and his pardoning me without duress would save me (from punishment in the Aakhirah)?" "Certainly," replied Hadhrat Umar (RA). "In that case," said Hadhrat Fayrooz (RA), "I make you the witness that I am giving my sword, my horse and thirty thousand of my wealth to this youngster as a gift." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to the youngster, "Your pardon has been rewarded (by Allaah in the Aakhirah), O brother of the Quraysh and you have also received plenty of wealth (in this world)."
sources: lbn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol. 7 Pg.83).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) .reports that a slave woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and said, "My master has accused me of fornication and made me sit on a fire until my private organ was burnt." Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked her, "Did anyone witness you commit the act?" When she replied in the negative, he asked further, "Did you make any confession before him?" When she again said that she did not, Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, "I shall deal with him." When Hadhrat Umar (RA) saw the man, he asked, "Do you punish with punishment that is reserved for Allaah (with fire)?!" The man entreated, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I was suspicious of her." "Did you see her commit the act?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) demanded to know. "No," came the reply, Hadhrat Umar enquired further, "Did she then confess to you that she committed the act?" Again he said, "No."

Hadhrat Umar (RA) then exclaimed, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life that I would have definitely taken retribution from you had I not heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Retribution cannot be taken from a master for anything he does to his slave and also not from a father for anything he does to his child.' Hadhrat Umar (RA) had the man lashed a hundred times and then said to the woman, "You may go because you are now freed for the pleasure of Allaah. You are now the freed slave of Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. I testify that I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The person who Is burnt by fire or disfigured by it is a free person and is the freed slave of Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ.
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat, lbn Asaakir and Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.299).

paras: Hadhrat Makhool narrates that Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) once called a non-Arab Christian farm labourer to ljold his animal next to Baytul Maqdas. When the labourer refused, Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) hit him so hard that his head was cut. The labourer sought help from Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) who then asked Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA), "What made you do that to him?" Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) replied, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! He refused to hold my animal when I asked him to do so, so I hit him because I am a short-tempered man." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then instructed Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) to sit down so that the labourer could have his revenge, just then, Hadhrat zaid bin Thaabit interrupted by saying, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Will you allow your slave to take revenge from your brother?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) then left out the retribution and determined that Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) should compensate the labourer in money.

Hadhrat Suwayd bin Ghafala (RA) reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once arrived in Shaam, a man belonging to the Ahlul Kitaab said to him, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! A man from amongst the Mu'mineen did this to me." The man's head was cut and he had been beaten. Hadhrat Umar (RA) became extremely angry and then said to Hadhrat Suhayb (RA), "Go and investigate who is responsible for this and then bring the culprit to me." Hadhrat Suhayb proceeded and discovered that the person responsible was Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik Ashja'ee. Hadhrat Suhayb (RA) said to Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik, "The Ameerul Mu'mineen is extremely angry with you. Bring along Mu'aadh bin jabal to speak to him because I fear that he will be very hasty in deciding your matter."

After Hadhrat Umar (RA) had completed his salaah, he called for Hadhrat Suhayb and asked him whether he had 'brought the person. "Yes," replied Hadhrat Suhayb (RA), In the meanwhile, Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) had already approached Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) and narrated the incident to him. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) then stood up and said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! The man is Awf bin Maalik. Please give him a hearing and do not be hasty with him." to Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) Hadhrat Umar SI asked, "What has happened between you and this person?" Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I sawthis man pushing along the donkey of a Muslim woman. He then poked the donkey so that it should throw her off, but it did not. He then pushed the donkey and it dropped her. Thereafter, he fell on to her (and raped her. Unable to bear this, I then hit him)." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Bring the woman to me so that she may confirm what you said." When Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) went to her, her father and her husband said, "What do you want with our woman? You have already disgraced us (by relating the story)." Howevtr, the woman said, "By Allaah! I shall definitely go with him!" Her father and husband then said, "We shall rather go and relate the incident on your behalf." The two men then went to Hadhrat Umar and related the story just as Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA) had. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then had the Jew crucified and said (to the Jewish (1) Bayhaqi, as quoted in Kama! Pg.303). population), "This (type of behaviour) was not amongst the clauses of our treaty with you." He then said, "O people! Fear Allaah with regard to those under the guardianship of Muhammad ﷺ (the Dhimmis), However, there shall be no guardianship for those of them who do this (who rape Muslim women)." Hadhrat Suwayd says that the Jew was the first person he had seen crucified in islaam.
sources: Abu Ubayd, Bayhaqi and ibn Asaakir, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.299). Tabraani has reported a similar narration in brief from Hadhrat Awf bin Maalik (RA), He has narrated from reliable sources, as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.6 Pg. 13). (2) lbn Mandah and Abu Nu'aym, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.7 Pg.13). ibn Abi Shaybah has also reported a similar narration from lmaam Sha'bi, as quoted in isaaba (Vol.1 Pg.52).

paras: Hadhrat Abdul Malik bin Ya'la Laythi narrates that Hadhrat Bakr bin Shaddaah Laythi used to serve Rasulullaah ﷺ when he was a child. After he came of age, he approached Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ I used to gq into the homes of your wives, but I have now reached the age of a man.

Rasulullaah till then prayed for him saying, "O Allaah! Make his speech always truthful and grant him success." it happened during the Khilaafah of Hadhrat umar (RA) that a Jew was found murdered. Hadhrat Umar (RA) regarded this to be a very serious matter and was very perturbed. He mounted the pulpit and said, "Will people be suddenly killed 'during the period in which Allaah has made me the Khalifah? In the name of Allaah do I beseech anyone with any knowledge (of the murder) to inform me likewise." Hadhrat Bakr bin Shaddaah (RA) then stood up and said, "It was I who did it." Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, "Allaahu Akbar! You are confessing to the murder! Explain your excuse." "Certainly," said Hadhrat Bakr bin Shaddaah "When a certain Muslim left to fight in Jihaad, he appointed me to the task of caring for his family. I came one day and found this Jew in the (Muslim's) house saying: "Islaam has deceived Ash 'ath (the Muslim out in Jihaad) so much that I have spent the entire night alone with his wife I spent the night on her breasts While she spent the night on bare-backed and lean camel It appears that at the place where her thighs meet Are waves crashing on to waves"
Hadhrat Umar (RA) believed Hadhrat Bakr bin Shaddaah (RA) because of the prayer of Rasulullaah iilf and acquitted him for the murder.

Hadhrat Qaasim bin Abi Bazza reports that a Muslim once killed a Dhimmi in Shaam. The case was brought before Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin jarraah (RA), who then wrote to Hadhrat Umar (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) wrote back with the instruction that if killing Dhimmis is a habitual practice of the Muslim, he should be executed. However, if he did it in a fit of rage, he should pay a penalty of four thousand Dirhams.
sources: Ibn Saa'id and Laalka'ee, as quoted in Kanzul ummaal (Vol.2 Pg.298).

paras: It is reported that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once wrote the following letter to one of the army commanders he had dispatched: "The news has reached me that some of your men seek out the burly Mushrikeen soldiers and even if they flee to the mountains where they feel safe, your men tell them 'Matras' (a Persian word meaning 'Have no fear', used to assure the person that he would not be harmed). Thereafter, when they have the man in custody (after he had given himself up upon the assurance of safety) they kill him. I swear by the Being Who controls my lifel If the news reaches me that any of you does this, I shall have him executed.

Another narration from Abu Salama states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life! If any of you points your finger towards the sty for any Mushrik (assuring him safety) and then kills him when he surrenders himself, I shall have him executed.
Hadhrat Anas SiP says, "When we laid siege to the city of Tustar, (their leader)

Hurmuzaan eventually surrendered on the verdict of Umar. I then brought him to Umar, When we arrived, Umar told Hurmuzaan to speak. Hurmuzaan asked, 'Should I speak like a dead man or like a living person?' Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "You may speak, 'Laa Ba's' (without fear).'

Hurmuzaan then said, 'O Arabs! As long as Allaah had left you and us to ourselves, we used to enslave you, kill you and usurp your wealth. However, since Allaah has been with you, we have no strength against you.'

"What have you to say?' Umar asked me. I said, 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I have left behind me a large enemy force, who have tremendous strength. If you kill him, his people will lose hope in living and their strength will be even greater (so do not kill him).' Umar said, 'Can I allow the murderer of (great people like) Baraa bin Maalik (the brother of Hadhrat Anas (RA) and Hajza bin Thowr to remain alive?'
